## Result
The fitted cooling rate is {{< meta cooling-fit.rate >}} with a linearized
standard error of {{< meta cooling-fit.rate-standard-error >}}, a time constant of
{{< meta cooling-fit.time-constant >}}, and a residual RMSE of
{{< meta cooling-fit.rmse >}} over {{< meta cooling-fit.observations >}} observations.
Numerical checks: {{< meta cooling-fit.checks >}}.
:::

## Question

What single first-order cooling rate $k$ ($\mathrm{s^{-1}}$) describes the
retained temperature observations when the ambient and initial temperatures are
fixed inputs?

## Model

The model assumes that the cooling rate is proportional to the temperature
difference from the surroundings, the relation usually attributed to
@newton1701:

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k\,(T - T_a)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T(t) = T_a + (T_0 - T_a)\,e^{-k t},
$$ {#eq-cooling-model}

with temperature $T$ in $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, time $t$ in $\mathrm{s}$, ambient
temperature $T_a$, and initial temperature $T_0$. The fit minimizes the sum of
squared temperature residuals subject to $k \ge 0$,

$$
\hat{k} = \arg\min_{k \ge 0} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left[T(t_i; k) - T_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\right]^2,
$$ {#eq-fit-objective}

using @eq-cooling-model for $T(t_i; k)$, solved with the SciPy
[@virtanen2020] trust-region reflective least-squares method [@branch1999]
from two initial guesses.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
The time constant $1/k$ is the time for the temperature excess $T - T_a$ to
fall by a factor of $e$.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumptions
- $T_a$ and $T_0$ are exact inputs from `inputs/parameters.json`; only $k$ is fitted.
- Temperature errors are independent with equal variance, and time is exact.
- One exponential rate describes the whole record (lumped, first-order cooling).
:::

## Results

@tbl-cooling-parameters reports the fitted rate at the minimum of
@eq-fit-objective. @fig-cooling-fit compares @eq-cooling-model with the
observations, and @fig-cooling-residuals and @tbl-cooling-data give the
remaining misfit at each observation time.

{{< include results/cooling_fit_include.qmd >}}

## Uncertainty

The standard error comes from the Jacobian $J_i = \partial T(t_i; k)/\partial k$
at the optimum,

$$
\mathrm{SE}(\hat{k}) = \sqrt{\frac{s^2}{\sum_i J_i^2}},
\qquad
s^2 = \frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i^2,
$$ {#eq-rate-standard-error}

and the 95 % interval in @tbl-cooling-parameters is
$\hat{k} \pm t_{0.975,\,n-1}\,\mathrm{SE}(\hat{k})$ from @eq-rate-standard-error.[^linearized]
The residual RMSE bound used by the numerical check is 5 % of the observed
temperature range; the refit tolerance scales with $\hat{k}$ (see the model
source below).

[^linearized]: This estimate linearizes the model around $\hat{k}$ and omits
    any uncertainty in $T_a$ and $T_0$, so the full uncertainty of $k$ can be
    larger than the interval shown.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Limitations
- The example observations carry no measurement record, instrument uncertainty,
  or sample description, so this fit demonstrates the method; it is not a
  physical validation of the cooling model.
- $T_0$ equals the first observation, so the fit does not test that input.
- A structured residual pattern would indicate that one rate is not enough;
  inspect @fig-cooling-residuals before relying on $k$.
:::
